newsitem.title: UK: UK in new call for urgent EU farm reform.
newsitem.headline: UK in new call for urgent EU farm reform.

text.p: UK Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg said reform is urgently needed in the beef, milk and cereals sectors of the European Union's Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) if EU farmers are not to lose crucial export markets.
Hogg said farmers should be allowed to throw off what he called the shackles of quotas and set-aside to allow them to compete in world markets.
Wholesale CAP reform was becoming inevitable because of the likely enlargement of the EU and a further round of trade talks on agriculture, he told an Agra Europe Outlook conference in London.
"By 2005, not only will we have concluded the world trade talks on agriculture but we will also have incorporated into the EU at least some eastern European countries.
"It is inconceivable that we will still, at that date, be imposing quotas, set-aside...whilst we carefully count our diminishing export rights."
